## Notes from the betting table

**This cycle is shorter than it looks.** Eight weeks of calendar, and the year-end shutdown takes
four working days out of the middle of it, so the capacity the room is betting against is a little
over seven build weeks and not eight. That subtraction is the reason the two bets in it are the
freeze and the rerun and nothing else: December is not where you start something.

**The freeze waits on cycle 37.** `pitch-7b3e94` depends on `pitch-6f2d18`, so nothing under it can
start until the scan operator has actually been lowered — freezing the backend API before one
operator has been through it end to end would be freezing a guess. The dependency is written once,
on the pitch, and the tasks under it inherit it; that is the shape the plan is meant to have, and
it is why neither task carries a `depends_on` of its own for it.

**The rerun is on the far side of the shutdown on purpose.** Stonechat picks the backend suite up
on the Monday before Christmas, and most of its span is the plant being shut. The room's view was
that a suite rerun is the one piece of work that survives being interrupted by a fortnight of
nobody touching it, so it is the piece that gets to straddle the closure.

**Left out: the operator set.** Lowering the remaining reductions was argued for and dropped. The
appetite for it depends entirely on how cycle 37's single scan goes, and a bet placed in November
against a number nobody has yet is a bet on the estimate rather than on the work.

*The availability figures above are invented. They are equal here and unequal in cycle 37 so that
the two records exercise different arithmetic on the way to a span.*
